episodes.title: Leaving a Religious Cult, Emotions as Sins, and Spiritual Bypassing
episodes.description:
Christy grew up homeschooled and was part of a cult for a large part of her childhood. The cult, founded by Bill Gothard, is known as the Institute in Basic Life Principles (IBLP). Gothard stepped down as leader when multiple sexual abuse allegations were made against him. The teachings and culture of the cult deeply influenced the way Christy saw her faith, the world, and her own identity.

In this episode, Christy shares how negative and uncomfortable emotions are weaponized within a cult. She explains how cults use power and control to prevent suspicion within the community. She discusses how strict standards are placed on women in particular and how freeing it felt to finally allowed herself to express her true personality after leaving IBLP.

We discuss the practice of "spiritual bypassing" and how damaging it is to suppress our emotions with religious platitudes. Christy also gives advice on how to interact with a friend who is in a cult or is spiritually bypassing.

Topics We Cover:
- Volunteering with baby goats
- Why uncomfortable emotions are not sins
- History of Bill Gothard, IBLP, and Advanced Training Institute (ATI)
- How cults use fear to control people
- Treatment of women within cults
- Finding your voice
- Spiritual bypassing
- Permission to feel and express emotions
- How to love someone who is trapped in a cult
- Doubt is not a sin
